name: Dorchester Cracker Plum Pudding
description: Historical recipe from Common Sense in the Household (1871). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: Nutmeg, cloves, and cinnamon to taste
ingredients.originalText: Nutmeg, cloves, and cinnamon to taste

ingredients.name: raisins, seeded and cut in two
ingredients.originalText: 1 lb. raisins, seeded and cut in two

instructions.text: Make a custard of the milk, eggs, and sugar, seasoned with the spices, by heating the milk almost to boiling, then taking it from the fire and adding gradually the yolks, sugar, seasoning, and whites.
Butter a pudding-dish; put a layer of crackers in the bottom, moistening with a few spoonfuls of the hot custard.
On this lay some of the raisins—a thick stratum; cover with crackers—the buttered side downward; moisten with the custard, and proceed in this order until your crackers and fruit are used up.
Pour in custard until only the top of the upper layer is visible, but not enough to float them.
Cover closely and set in the cellar over night.
In the morning add the rest of the custard, at intervals of five or six minutes between the cupfuls.
Bake two hours in a moderate oven.
Cover with paper if it should seem likely to harden too fast.

source.author: Marion Harland
source.originalInstructions:
1. Make a custard of the milk, eggs, and sugar, seasoned with the spices, by heating the milk almost to boiling, then taking it from the fire and adding gradually the yolks, sugar, seasoning, and whites.
2. Do not boil it again.
3. Butter a pudding-dish; put a layer of crackers in the bottom, moistening with a few spoonfuls of the hot custard.
4. On this lay some of the raisins—a thick stratum; cover with crackers—the buttered side downward; moisten with the custard, and proceed in this order until your crackers and fruit are used up.
5. Pour in custard until only the top of the upper layer is visible, but not enough to float them.
6. Cover closely and set in the cellar over night.
7. In the morning add the rest of the custard, at intervals of five or six minutes between the cupfuls.
8. Bake two hours in a moderate oven.
9. Cover with paper if it should seem likely to harden too fast.
10. Eat hot, with sauce.
